title: Blocking Basics
description: Finish your crochet neatly by shaping, smoothing, and setting the fabric.

content.summary: Blocking uses moisture and shaping to relax the stitches, improve drape, and make edges cleaner.
content.whyItMatters: Blocking helps lace open up, granny squares match size better, and finished pieces look more intentional.
steps: Check the fiber content so you know whether wet, steam, or spray blocking is safe.
Dampen the project evenly without soaking it more than needed.
Shape the piece to the intended dimensions on a flat surface.
Pin edges or corners if you need sharper structure.
Let the project dry fully before removing pins.
content.practice: Block one small swatch or square so you can compare the before and after shape.
commonMistakes: Stretching the fabric too aggressively while pinning.
Removing the piece before it is fully dry.
